# Chromobench DSL reference

Globals: `cb`, `frame`, `units`, `mem`, `console`; the builders `layer`, `group`, `mask`, `coll`; the changes `set`, `insert`, `remove`, `move`. A frame is a document (format 3: stages with a medium and a stack of layers and groups, a mask library, geometry, output). Its cuts are image handles: lazy nodes of the one compiler; `await` a measurement for numbers. Options are literal values. A what-if is `frame.with(change)`; `frame.propose(change, { why })` submits a change when the eval succeeds.

## Vocabulary

- `frame.print() · frame.cut('darkroom.H') · source() scan() scene() film() negative() finished() display()` — a cut of the frame's compiled document: an image handle (the node the viewer and the export name)
- `frame.doc · frame.get('main.params.time_s')` — the document as the eval started (read-only); get reads one path, id-anchored like set
- `frame.with(set('main.params.time_s', 12)).print()` — a what-if: the document with a change, compiled by the one compiler; changes nothing
- `frame.propose(change, { why, label })` — validates a change now and submits it when the eval succeeds (ask: a proposal; auto: applied); the receipt has a preview what-if
- `frame.why('main.params.time_s') · frame.pending()` — who set a value, and from where; the proposals waiting for the photographer
- `frame.explain()` — the document: stages with media, laws and entries (with the nodes they compile to), masks, geometry
- `layer('burn', { stops: 0.5 }).amount(0.5).mask('sky') · .blend .name .enabled .params` — a layer value: an op of a stage stack with amount, mask and blend
- `group('Sky', { b1: layer('burn', { stops: 0.5 }) }).amount(0.6)` — a group value: entries that act as one (keys are their ids, in order)
- `mask('sky').add('c1', 'linear', { from, to }).add('c2', 'luminance', { above: 0.5 }, 'intersect').feather(1)` — a mask value: components (add = max, subtract, intersect = product), feather in mm, invert, reads
- `set(path, v) · insert(coll, id, item, at?) · remove(id) · move(id, { into, at }) · [a, b]` — the four mutations, as change values; several changes are an array, applied in order
- `coll({ s1: { … }, s2: { … } })` — a collection (a list argument such as heal spots or paint strokes): keys are ids, in order
- `h.show('label' | { label, box, at, size })` — shows you an image with the numbers it shows (max 4 per eval)
- `cb.compare([a, b], 'label')` — one side-by-side image; each half carries its own numbers
- `cb.testStrip(frame, { vary: 'time', steps: 7, step: 1 / 3 })` — a test strip of the negative; its image carries one reading per band
- `cb.ringAround(frame, { step_pt: 4 })` — a 3×3 ring-around; its image carries one reading per cell
- `cb.looks.apply(name, params, { amount, to, where, why }) · whatIf(frame, name, params) · diff(a, b) · bake(link) · list()` — registered looks and presets as links on the frames: what-ifs, diffs, one proposal batch over frames, bake
- `units.pt(x) · toPt · stops · toStops · stopsFromTime(t1, t2) · stopsFromFstop(n1, n2)` — unit conversions; numbers or arrays

## Cuts

Named points of the compiled document, in pipeline order; a frame has those of its kind.

- `frame.source()` → camera-linear — The decoded source as opened (source.open): linear sensor values.
- `frame.scan()` → scanner-density (negative-scan only) — The scan in scanner density after the scan stage (flat field, flare, density, dust heal).
- `frame.cut('scene.input')` → scene-xyz (digital-raw only) — The scene in XYZ after white balance, before the scene stage: what the scene stage's masks measure.
- `frame.scene()` → scene-xyz (digital-raw only) — The scene in XYZ after white balance and the scene stage: what the film is exposed to.
- `frame.film()` → film-dyes (digital-raw only) — The developed film of a camera file (after film.grain): its negative.
- `frame.negative()` → film-dyes — The negative in dye amounts: the darkroom's input (invert.dyes of a scan, the film of a camera file).
- `frame.cut('darkroom.main')` → paper-logH — The main exposure alone (print.expose of the entry main), before any other darkroom entry.
- `frame.cut('darkroom.H')` → paper-logH — Paper log exposure after the light law (every darkroom entry), before development.
- `frame.print()` → print-xyz — The print under the viewing light, adapted (view.adapt), before the print stage.
- `frame.finished()` → print-xyz — The print after the print stage (retouch, clarity, digital layers).
- `frame.display()` → display-rgb — Display RGB after output.display and the document geometry (output.frame).

## Paths

A path is dotted. It starts at an item id (`main.params.time_s`, `sky.feather_mm`: ids are unique in the document and survive moves) or at a root key (`stages.darkroom.medium.paper`, `geometry.crop`). Collections are crossed by item id (`masks.sky.name`); `order` and `items` never appear. A new document has the darkroom entries `main` (expose: time_s, fstop, filtration) and `lights` (filter: logH, the printer lights).

- `set(path, value)` sets a field
- `insert(coll, id, item, at?)` adds an item to a collection: a stack (`stages.print.stack`, `<group>.stack`), the mask library (`masks`), a list argument (`<layer>.params.spots`)
- `remove(id)` deletes an item wherever it is
- `move(id, { into, at })` reorders it, or moves it into another collection

## Stages

### scan (negative-scan)

Negative scans: scanner, stock and base; heal and clone on the negative (dust).

Law **repair**: amount opacity in [0, 1]; no blend modes; groups pass; order stack. Scan: entries apply in order, each replacing pixels within its geometry (heal and clone spots on the negative). Amount is opacity; no blend modes.

Medium (`stages.scan.medium`):

- `stages.scan.medium.scanner`: string — Scanner model.
- `stages.scan.medium.stock`: stockId — Film stock.
- `stages.scan.medium.format`: enum 135|645|66|67|45 — Film format.
- `stages.scan.medium.umPerPx`: number, um — Film µm per document pixel: the scan medium's umPerPx, or a camera file's film format over its long side. Sets ImageInfo.umPerPx.film, which every physical size (µm on the film, mm on the print) is converted with.
- `stages.scan.medium.rebate`: box, px — Box in source (sensor) pixels; absent means automatic.
- `stages.scan.medium.baseT`: vec3, fraction — Linear value of the film base (the roll's, from roll setup); wins over rebate. Absent = measure on the rebate box.
- `stages.scan.medium.flat`: string — SHA-256 of the flat-field frame (opened like a source).
- `stages.scan.medium.openGate`: a box, "flat" or null (document px)
- `stages.scan.medium.flare`: number, percent — Scanner veiling flare f, percent of the open-gate signal; [r, g, b] is per channel (ingest fitFlare / filmLayout measure it per channel).

Layers (`insert('stages.scan.stack', id, layer(op, params))`):

- `layer('clone', { spots }) in scan, print — Clones circular spots: the source patch replaces the target as it is.`
  - spots: list, default [] — Spots in order; each reads the image as the spots before it left it (in a document: a Coll of spots).
- `layer('heal', { spots }) in scan, print — Heals circular spots: the source patch, matched to the target's surroundings, replaces the target (dust on the negative in the scan stage, blemishes on the print).`
  - spots: list, default [] — Spots in order; each reads the image as the spots before it left it (in a document: a Coll of spots).

### scene (digital-raw)

Camera files: white balance; digital adjustments before the film (scene-linear).

Law **composite**: amount opacity in [0, 1]; blend modes; groups pass, isolated; order stack. Scene and print: entries apply bottom to top, v ← v + a·m·(B(v, A(v)) − v) in the op's encoding (XYZ, linear RGB or OkLab; the compiler converts between them). Amount is opacity. A pass group's children act on the backdrop and the group fades their total effect; an isolated group blends its children's result as one layer with its mode.

Medium (`stages.scene.medium`):

- `stages.scene.medium.whiteBalance.temperature_K`: number, K — White balance: the temperature of the light the scene was lit by (Lightroom's Temperature; higher makes the picture warmer). Default: no correction (D65).
- `stages.scene.medium.whiteBalance.tint`: number — White balance: the light's tint, green (−) to magenta (+) correction, in Lightroom's units (Adobe's: 1 = 1/3000 of a CIE 1960 uv unit across the isotemperature line).

Layers (`insert('stages.scene.stack', id, layer(op, params))`):

- `layer('curve', { channel, points }) in scene, print — A point curve (Lightroom's point curve, Photoshop's Curves) on lightness or one channel.`
  - channel: enum L|R|G|B, default "L" — What the tone function maps: L = OkLab lightness (tone without hue shifts); R, G, B = the cube root of that linear RGB channel, the same lightness scale (a neutral's R, G and B curves are its L curve).
  - points: list, default [{"x":0,"y":0},{"x":1,"y":1}] — Control points in order of x (in a document: a Coll of points). The curve is the monotone cubic through them (Fritsch–Carlson): it never overshoots, so monotone points give a monotone curve; beyond the end points it continues along the end tangents.
- `layer('exposure', { stops, offset }) in scene, print — Exposure in linear light: rgb · 2^stops + offset (Editor lab `exposure`, without its sRGB round trip and gamma).`
  - stops: number, stop, [-6, 6], default 0 — Exposure change: linear RGB × 2^stops.
  - offset: number, fraction, [-0.2, 0.2], default 0 — Added after the gain, a fraction of white (a black level: negative removes a veil).
- `layer('grade', { shadowsHue_deg, shadowsChroma, shadowsLightness, midtonesHue_deg, midtonesChroma, midtonesLightness, highlightsHue_deg, highlightsChroma, highlightsLightness, balance }) in scene, print — Colour grading with shadow, midtone and highlight wheels in OkLab (Lightroom's Color Grading): weights (1 − t)², 2t(1 − t), t² of the lightness, a, b += L·Σ w·chroma·(cos hue, sin hue), L += 0.25·Σ w·lightness.`
  - shadowsHue_deg: number, deg, [0, 360], default 230 — Shadows: the OkLCh hue of the tint.
  - shadowsChroma: number, [0, 0.3], default 0 — Shadows: the tint's strength, OkLab chroma added at L = 1 (scaled by L, so black stays black).
  - shadowsLightness: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0 — Shadows: lightness change, ΔL = 0.25 · lightness · weight.
  - midtonesHue_deg: number, deg, [0, 360], default 60 — Midtones: the OkLCh hue of the tint.
  - midtonesChroma: number, [0, 0.3], default 0 — Midtones: the tint's strength, OkLab chroma added at L = 1 (scaled by L, so black stays black).
  - midtonesLightness: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0 — Midtones: lightness change, ΔL = 0.25 · lightness · weight.
  - highlightsHue_deg: number, deg, [0, 360], default 70 — Highlights: the OkLCh hue of the tint.
  - highlightsChroma: number, [0, 0.3], default 0 — Highlights: the tint's strength, OkLab chroma added at L = 1 (scaled by L, so black stays black).
  - highlightsLightness: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0 — Highlights: lightness change, ΔL = 0.25 · lightness · weight.
  - balance: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0 — Moves the split between the wheels: positive gives the highlights more of the range (t = clamp(L, 0, 1)^(2^−balance)).
- `layer('hsl', { bands }) in scene, print — Hue, saturation and lightness per hue band in OkLCh (Lightroom's HSL panel); replaces the never-compiled finishing.hue.`
  - bands: list, default [{"centre_deg":25,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":55,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":105,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":145,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":195,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":260,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":295,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":330,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0}] — Hue bands (in a document: a Coll; default the eight of Lightroom's HSL panel: red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, purple, magenta). A band weighs a pixel by w = smoothstep(cos width, 1, cos(h − centre)); weights are normalised by max(1, Σw) and faded towards neutral (chroma below 0.04).
- `layer('levels', { channel, black, white, gamma, outBlack, outWhite }) in scene, print — Levels on lightness or one channel: out = outBlack + (outWhite − outBlack)·g((x − black)/(white − black)), g(t) = t^(1/gamma) on [0, 1] and continued with slope 1 beyond, so nothing is clipped in the working encoding (the display knee clips).`
  - channel: enum L|R|G|B, default "L" — What the tone function maps: L = OkLab lightness (tone without hue shifts); R, G, B = the cube root of that linear RGB channel, the same lightness scale (a neutral's R, G and B curves are its L curve).
  - black: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0 — Input black point (the channel's lightness).
  - white: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 1 — Input white point.
  - gamma: number, [0.1, 10], default 1 — Midtone gamma: t^(1/gamma) between black and white (above 1 brightens).
  - outBlack: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0 — Output black: where the input black lands.
  - outWhite: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 1 — Output white: where the input white lands.
- `layer('mixer', { red, green, blue, monochrome, grey }) in scene, print — A 3 × 3 channel mixer in linear RGB, or black and white from weighted channels (Editor lab `bw`, generalised and in linear light).`
  - red: vec3, fraction, [-2, 2], default [1,0,0] — Output red from input R, G, B (linear RGB).
  - green: vec3, fraction, [-2, 2], default [0,1,0] — Output green from input R, G, B.
  - blue: vec3, fraction, [-2, 2], default [0,0,1] — Output blue from input R, G, B.
  - monochrome: bool, default false — Black and white: every channel becomes grey = grey · (R, G, B); the rows are not used.
  - grey: vec3, fraction, [-2, 2], default [0.2627,0.678,0.0593] — Weights of R, G, B in the monochrome grey (default the luminance of Rec. 2020: a neutral conversion; filters shift them, as a red filter on panchromatic film).
- `layer('vibrance', { vibrance, saturation }) in scene, print — Vibrance and saturation in OkLCh chroma (Editor lab `vibrance`, in chroma instead of an sRGB spread).`
  - vibrance: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0.25 — Chroma change weighted to muted colours: C × (1 + v·(1 − C/0.3)²) below C = 0.3 (monotone: colours keep their order).
  - saturation: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0 — Uniform chroma change after vibrance: C × (1 + saturation).
- `layer('vignette', { stops, size, feather }) in scene, print — A vignette in linear light, centred on the frame (document pixels): rgb · 2^(stops · smoothstep(size, size + feather·(1 − size), ρ)), ρ = 1 at the corners.`
  - stops: number, stop, [-4, 4], default -0.5 — Exposure change at the corners (negative darkens).
  - size: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0.5 — Where the falloff starts, a fraction of the distance from the centre to the corners on the frame's ellipse.
  - feather: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0.5 — How much of the rest of the way the falloff takes (0: a hard edge, 1: it reaches the corners).

### film (digital-raw)

Camera files: the film the scene is shot on and its development.

No law: the stage takes no entries yet.

Medium (`stages.film.medium`):

- `stages.film.medium.stock`: stockId — Film stock the scene is shot on.
- `stages.film.medium.exposureEV`: number, stop — Exposure relative to the stock reference.
- `stages.film.medium.format.longEdge_mm`: number, mm — Long edge of the simulated film format; over the source's long side it is the film pitch.
- `stages.film.medium.push`: number, stop — Push (+) or pull (−) development.
- `stages.film.medium.dir.amount`: number, fraction — DIR coupler strength.
- `stages.film.medium.dir.diffusion_um`: number, um — DIR diffusion length.
- `stages.film.medium.halation.strength`: number, fraction — Halation strength relative to the stock.
- `stages.film.medium.grain.amount`: number, fraction — Grain amount relative to the stock.
- `stages.film.medium.grain.size_um`: number, um — Grain clump size.
- `stages.film.medium.grain.seed`: number — Seed; grain is a pure function of inputs, seed and print grid, independent of tiling.

### darkroom (every frame)

The enlarger and the paper: light on the paper (exposures, dodges, burns, flashes, masks, filters).

Law **light**: amount scale in [0, 16]; no blend modes; groups pass; order free. Darkroom: every entry is light on the paper (expose, burn, dodge, flash, preflash) or a filter in its path (densityMask, filter); they add in linear H and multiply transmissions, so the order is free. Amount scales a contribution's light and a modulator's density; groups multiply their children's amounts and masks.

Medium (`stages.darkroom.medium`):

- `stages.darkroom.medium.paper`: stockId — Colour paper (darkroom medium).
- `stages.darkroom.medium.aim`: enum grey-0.184|midgray-normalised — What printer lights 0 mean: the grey card prints as a neutral 0.184 reflectance (grey-0.184), or the normalised mid-grey exposure alone.
- `stages.darkroom.medium.mode`: enum real|normalised — real: a physical enlarger, where time, aperture and magnification expose the paper (CHB-010; the default since contract 0.4, CHB-031); normalised: the grey card prints at the aim at lights 0 whatever the optics, so time, aperture and magnification do nothing.
- `stages.darkroom.medium.lamp`: string — Enlarger lamp and heat filter.
- `stages.darkroom.medium.magnification`: number — Enlarger magnification: light ∝ 1/(m + 1)² in real mode (8 = the calibration's reference), and the print's pitch: ImageInfo.umPerPx.paper = umPerPx.film × m (CHB-010; contract 1.0: always given).
- `stages.darkroom.medium.grade`: number — Contrast grade: a gamma about the aim grey, so the grey card stays (0 → 0.7, 1 → 0.82, 2 → 1 the paper as made, 3 → 1.2, 4 → 1.45, 5 → 1.8). Colour papers have no grades; this is a contrast control (darkroom medium).

Layers (`insert('stages.darkroom.stack', id, layer(op, params))`):

- `layer('burn', { time_s, stops, filtration }) in darkroom — More light through the negative under a mask (a split exposure is a burn with its own filtration).`
  - time_s: number, s, [0, 600], optional — Seconds of light (absolute). Give time_s or stops, not both.
  - stops: number, stop, [0, 6], optional — Relative to the main time: burn and flash t_main·(2^s − 1), dodge t_main·(1 − 2^−s). Give time_s or stops, not both.
  - filtration: cmy, CC, [-100, 200], optional — The exposure's own pack, a shift on the database neutral like the main exposure's filtration; absent = the main exposure's.
- `layer('densityMask', { gamma, radius_um, polarity }) in darkroom — A neutral silver mask made from the negative and sandwiched with it (CHB-010 §6.6): every exposure through the negative passes its density, flashes do not.`
  - gamma: number, [0, 1], default 0.5 — Mask gamma γ_m (0.6: large-area contrast falls to 40 %).
  - radius_um: number, um, [0, 5000], default 300 — Gaussian σ of the blur on the film: wide for a contrast mask, a thin spacer for an unsharp mask.
  - polarity: enum positive|same, default "positive" — positive lowers large-area contrast; same raises it.
- `layer('dodge', { time_s, stops }) in darkroom — Light held back from the main exposure under a mask (never more than the main gives: max(E_main − Σ E_dodge, 0)).`
  - time_s: number, s, [0, 600], optional — Seconds of light (absolute). Give time_s or stops, not both.
  - stops: number, stop, [0, 6], optional — Relative to the main time: burn and flash t_main·(2^s − 1), dodge t_main·(1 − 2^−s). Give time_s or stops, not both.
- `layer('expose', { time_s, fstop, filtration }) in darkroom — The main exposure through the negative: exactly one per document, id `main`.`
  - time_s: number, s, [0.1, 600], default 10 — Exposure time.
  - fstop: number, fstop, [2.8, 45], default 8 — Enlarger lens aperture (every exposure through the lens uses it).
  - filtration: cmy, CC, [-100, 200], default {"c":0,"m":0,"y":0} — Dichroic filtration as a shift on the database neutral pack for (paper, film); 0 = neutral.
- `layer('filter', { logH }) in darkroom — A filter in the light path: the printer lights, or a local colour correction in log H under a mask.`
  - logH: vec3, logH, [-1.5, 1.5], default [0,0,0] — Offsets of paper log exposure per layer (R, G, B light): H ← H·10^(a·m·logH). Never a density offset (Hunt 14.17).
- `layer('flash', { time_s, stops, filtration, through }) in darkroom — Light that does not pass the image: uniform under its mask, not held back by density masks.`
  - time_s: number, s, [0, 600], optional — Seconds of light (absolute). Give time_s or stops, not both.
  - stops: number, stop, [0, 6], optional — Relative to the main time: burn and flash t_main·(2^s − 1), dodge t_main·(1 − 2^−s). Give time_s or stops, not both.
  - filtration: cmy, CC, [-100, 200], optional — The exposure's own pack, a shift on the database neutral like the main exposure's filtration; absent = the main exposure's.
  - through: enum base|open, default "base" — Through the film base (no image: dye amounts 0) or an empty gate (no film).
- `layer('preflash', { fraction }) in darkroom — A uniform pre-exposure of the paper, added after the filters (it is measured against the grey card's exposure, H = 1 at the aim): H ← H + a·m·φ.`
  - fraction: number, fraction, [0, 0.2], default 0.02 — Uniform pre-exposure as a fraction of the grey-card exposure.

### print (every frame)

The print under the viewing light: retouch, clarity, digital layers (print-referred).

Law **composite**: amount opacity in [0, 1]; blend modes; groups pass, isolated; order stack. Scene and print: entries apply bottom to top, v ← v + a·m·(B(v, A(v)) − v) in the op's encoding (XYZ, linear RGB or OkLab; the compiler converts between them). Amount is opacity. A pass group's children act on the backdrop and the group fades their total effect; an isolated group blends its children's result as one layer with its mode.

Medium (`stages.print.medium`):

- `stages.print.medium.illuminant`: string — Viewing light.
- `stages.print.medium.flare`: number, percent — Viewing flare, percent of the paper white (0.48 % is the textbook value, §2.7).

Layers (`insert('stages.print.stack', id, layer(op, params))`):

- `layer('clarity', { strength, radius_mm }) in print — Local contrast on the print (a large unsharp mask weighted to the midtones): the low-pass of the print's luminance in linear light, the detail in lightness.`
  - strength: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0.25 — Local contrast: positive adds, negative softens.
  - radius_mm: number, mm, [0.1, 100], default 10 — Radius of the low-pass on the print, mm (converted with ImageInfo.umPerPx.paper, so it is the same at every export size).

  - spots: list, default [] — Spots in order; each reads the image as the spots before it left it (in a document: a Coll of spots).

  - shadowsHue_deg: number, deg, [0, 360], default 230 — Shadows: the OkLCh hue of the tint.
  - shadowsChroma: number, [0, 0.3], default 0 — Shadows: the tint's strength, OkLab chroma added at L = 1 (scaled by L, so black stays black).
  - shadowsLightness: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0 — Shadows: lightness change, ΔL = 0.25 · lightness · weight.
  - midtonesHue_deg: number, deg, [0, 360], default 60 — Midtones: the OkLCh hue of the tint.
  - midtonesChroma: number, [0, 0.3], default 0 — Midtones: the tint's strength, OkLab chroma added at L = 1 (scaled by L, so black stays black).
  - midtonesLightness: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0 — Midtones: lightness change, ΔL = 0.25 · lightness · weight.
  - highlightsHue_deg: number, deg, [0, 360], default 70 — Highlights: the OkLCh hue of the tint.
  - highlightsChroma: number, [0, 0.3], default 0 — Highlights: the tint's strength, OkLab chroma added at L = 1 (scaled by L, so black stays black).
  - highlightsLightness: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0 — Highlights: lightness change, ΔL = 0.25 · lightness · weight.
  - balance: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0 — Moves the split between the wheels: positive gives the highlights more of the range (t = clamp(L, 0, 1)^(2^−balance)).
- `layer('heal', { spots }) in scan, print — Heals circular spots: the source patch, matched to the target's surroundings, replaces the target (dust on the negative in the scan stage, blemishes on the print).`
  - spots: list, default [] — Spots in order; each reads the image as the spots before it left it (in a document: a Coll of spots).
- `layer('hsl', { bands }) in scene, print — Hue, saturation and lightness per hue band in OkLCh (Lightroom's HSL panel); replaces the never-compiled finishing.hue.`
  - bands: list, default [{"centre_deg":25,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":55,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":105,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":145,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":195,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":260,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":295,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0},{"centre_deg":330,"width_deg":45,"hue_deg":0,"saturation":0,"lightness":0}] — Hue bands (in a document: a Coll; default the eight of Lightroom's HSL panel: red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, purple, magenta). A band weighs a pixel by w = smoothstep(cos width, 1, cos(h − centre)); weights are normalised by max(1, Σw) and faded towards neutral (chroma below 0.04).
- `layer('levels', { channel, black, white, gamma, outBlack, outWhite }) in scene, print — Levels on lightness or one channel: out = outBlack + (outWhite − outBlack)·g((x − black)/(white − black)), g(t) = t^(1/gamma) on [0, 1] and continued with slope 1 beyond, so nothing is clipped in the working encoding (the display knee clips).`
  - channel: enum L|R|G|B, default "L" — What the tone function maps: L = OkLab lightness (tone without hue shifts); R, G, B = the cube root of that linear RGB channel, the same lightness scale (a neutral's R, G and B curves are its L curve).
  - black: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0 — Input black point (the channel's lightness).
  - white: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 1 — Input white point.
  - gamma: number, [0.1, 10], default 1 — Midtone gamma: t^(1/gamma) between black and white (above 1 brightens).
  - outBlack: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0 — Output black: where the input black lands.
  - outWhite: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 1 — Output white: where the input white lands.
- `layer('mixer', { red, green, blue, monochrome, grey }) in scene, print — A 3 × 3 channel mixer in linear RGB, or black and white from weighted channels (Editor lab `bw`, generalised and in linear light).`
  - red: vec3, fraction, [-2, 2], default [1,0,0] — Output red from input R, G, B (linear RGB).
  - green: vec3, fraction, [-2, 2], default [0,1,0] — Output green from input R, G, B.
  - blue: vec3, fraction, [-2, 2], default [0,0,1] — Output blue from input R, G, B.
  - monochrome: bool, default false — Black and white: every channel becomes grey = grey · (R, G, B); the rows are not used.
  - grey: vec3, fraction, [-2, 2], default [0.2627,0.678,0.0593] — Weights of R, G, B in the monochrome grey (default the luminance of Rec. 2020: a neutral conversion; filters shift them, as a red filter on panchromatic film).
- `layer('sharpen', { strength, radius_mm }) in print — An unsharp mask on the print's lightness (clarity without the midtone weight, at a small radius): the low-pass of Y in linear light, L = (Y / Y_w)^⅓, out = XYZ·(L′/L)³ (chromaticity kept, no clipping).`
  - strength: number, fraction, [0, 3], default 0.5 — Sharpening: the lightness detail added, L′ = L + s·(L − L̄).
  - radius_mm: number, mm, [0.01, 2], default 0.1 — Radius (Gaussian σ) of the low-pass on the print, mm (converted with ImageInfo.umPerPx.paper, so it is the same at every export size).
- `layer('vibrance', { vibrance, saturation }) in scene, print — Vibrance and saturation in OkLCh chroma (Editor lab `vibrance`, in chroma instead of an sRGB spread).`
  - vibrance: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0.25 — Chroma change weighted to muted colours: C × (1 + v·(1 − C/0.3)²) below C = 0.3 (monotone: colours keep their order).
  - saturation: number, fraction, [-1, 1], default 0 — Uniform chroma change after vibrance: C × (1 + saturation).
- `layer('vignette', { stops, size, feather }) in scene, print — A vignette in linear light, centred on the frame (document pixels): rgb · 2^(stops · smoothstep(size, size + feather·(1 − size), ρ)), ρ = 1 at the corners.`
  - stops: number, stop, [-4, 4], default -0.5 — Exposure change at the corners (negative darkens).
  - size: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0.5 — Where the falloff starts, a fraction of the distance from the centre to the corners on the frame's ellipse.
  - feather: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0.5 — How much of the rest of the way the falloff takes (0: a hard edge, 1: it reaches the corners).

## Masks

`mask(name).add(id, kind, params, combine, amount)`; combine add | subtract | intersect (add = max, subtract = a·(1 − b), intersect = a·b); `.feather(mm)` on the print; `.invert()`; `.reads(cut)` (default: the input of the stage that uses it). Geometry in document pixels. An entry uses a mask by id: `layer(…).mask('sky')`, after `insert('masks', 'sky', mask(…))`.

- `linear` { from, to } — Mask component 'linear': 1 at `from`, 0 at `to`, linear between, constant beyond (a graduated burn).
  - from: point, px, default {"x":0,"y":0} — Where the mask is 1 (document px).
  - to: point, px, default {"x":0,"y":100} — Where the mask is 0 (document px).
- `radial` { box, angle_deg, feather } — Mask component 'radial': an ellipse with its own soft edge (Lightroom's radial gradient), pointwise: no blur, unlike the mask's feather.
  - box: box, px, default {"x":0,"y":0,"w":16,"h":16} — Bounding box of the outer ellipse in document px (before rotation).
  - angle_deg: number, deg, [-90, 90], default 0 — Rotation about the box centre.
  - feather: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0.5 — Soft edge as a fraction of the radius: 1 inside the ellipse scaled by 1 − feather, 0 from the outer ellipse on, a smoothstep between.
- `ellipse` { box, angle_deg } — Mask component 'ellipse': the ellipse inscribed in the box.
  - box: box, px, default {"x":0,"y":0,"w":16,"h":16} — Bounding box in document px (before rotation).
  - angle_deg: number, deg, [-90, 90], default 0 — Rotation about the box centre.
- `paint` { strokes } — Mask component 'paint': brush strokes rasterised with soft round dabs.
  - strokes: list, default [] — Brush strokes in order (in a document: a Coll of strokes).
- `luminance` { above, below, softness } — Mask component 'luminance': how far the receiver's luminance (the mean of its channels, normalised to its domain range) lies inside [above, below].
  - above: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0 — Select values above this (normalised to the domain range). 0 means no lower bound (values below the domain range stay selected).
  - below: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 1 — Select values below this. 1 means no upper bound.
  - softness: number, fraction, [0, 0.5], default 0.05 — Transition width.
- `colour` { colour, tolerance, softness } — Mask component 'colour': how close the image's colour is to a sample, 1 − smoothstep(tolerance, tolerance + softness, ΔE_OK) (Editor lab's colour range, in OkLab ΔE instead of an RGB distance).
  - colour: vec3, [-0.5, 1.5], default [0.7,0,0] — The colour to select, OkLab (L, a, b) (the eyedropper reads it from the image the mask measures).
  - tolerance: number, [0, 1], default 0.1 — OkLab distance ΔE within which the mask is 1.
  - softness: number, [0, 1], default 0.05 — Distance over which it falls to 0 beyond the tolerance (a smoothstep).

## Workbench

The studio, as the photographer sees and drives it. Every `wb` call is answered by the studio: `await` it. A command
you run is the one a key runs, by you: in ask mode its changes to a document wait for approval, in auto mode they
apply (undoable), read-only refuses them; its effect shows in your next eval's reads and at once in `wb.state`.

- `await wb.commands(filter?)` — every command: `{ id, label, args, keys: [{ chord, args }], menu, enabled, why, hidden, checked }`
- `await wb.run(id, ...args)` — runs it: `{ ok, why, how: committed | proposed | refused | none, entries, module, frame }`
- `await wb.set(statePath, value)` — writes a state path as a bound control does (`view.view`, `finish.spot.r`)
- `await wb.selectors()`, `await wb.state(name, ...args)` — the typed selectors (`current`, `frame`, `doc`, `library`, `roll.frames`, …)
- `await wb.screen({ module? })` — `{ layout, module, modules, frame, tool, text, controls }`; each control says what it writes: `path` (+ `frame`: frame.propose(set(path, v))), `state` (wb.set) or `command` (+ `args`: wb.run); `await wb.screen().explain()` is the live text
- `await wb.layout()`, `await wb.layouts.list()` — the layout on screen; the ones to switch to (`wb.run('view.layout', id)` where the studio has it)
- `await wb.layouts.build({ id, label, description, build: (ck, cb, env) => cb.studio(name)… })` — `{ ok, errors, warnings, explain, controls, layout }`: the build runs here on recording proxies (the same ck and cb as the studio's layouts), the studio builds the recording and runs its passes
- `await wb.layouts.use(layout, { why })` — asks the photographer to switch to it (a dialog); keep `layout` on `mem` to revise it
- `await cb.looks.define(src)` — registers a look written as a `.cblook.js` source (`defineLook({ name, version, label, params, stages, fn })`) here and in the studio; then `cb.looks.apply(name)`

In a layout, functions do not cross: a state lambda is a selector `cb.sel.frame.print()` (calls after the name apply
to its result; `.not()`, `.eq(v)`, `.or(v)`, `.where({ field: v })` combine), a state path `cb.state.view.step`, a
handler a command id (`'frame.pick'`, `['frame.rate', 3]`); `.with(x => …)` and plain JavaScript (`map`, `?:`) run
at build time. A function where an option goes is E_LAYOUT. A module declares its stages (`stages: ['darkroom']`).

    - above: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0 — Select values above this (normalised to the domain range). 0 means no lower bound (values below the domain range stay selected).
    - below: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 1 — Select values below this. 1 means no upper bound.

  - `h.mask.paint({ strokes }) → mask — Mask component 'paint': brush strokes rasterised with soft round dabs.`

  - `h.mask.radial({ box, angle_deg, feather }) → mask — Mask component 'radial': an ellipse with its own soft edge (Lightroom's radial gradient), pointwise: no blur, unlike the mask's feather.`
    - box: box, px, default {"x":0,"y":0,"w":16,"h":16} — Bounding box of the outer ellipse in document px (before rotation).
    - angle_deg: number, deg, [-90, 90], default 0 — Rotation about the box centre.
    - feather: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0.5 — Soft edge as a fraction of the radius: 1 inside the ellipse scaled by 1 − feather, 0 from the outer ellipse on, a smoothstep between.
- **measure**
  - `h.measure.histogram({ channel, bins }) → value — Histogram over the domain range.`
    - channel: enum r|g|b|L, default "L" — Channel (L = mean of channels).
    - bins: number, [8, 1024], default 64 — Number of bins.
    - returns `edges`, `counts`
  - `h.measure.patches({ box, cols, rows }) → value — Mean value per grid cell (test strips, ring-arounds, charts).`
    - box: box, px, optional — Region; absent = whole image.
    - cols: number, [1, 24], default 1 — Columns.
    - rows: number, [1, 24], default 1 — Rows.
    - returns `cells`
  - `h.measure.stats({ box, mask }) → value — Exact statistics over a region.`
    - box: box, px, optional — Region in source px; absent = whole image.
    - mask: Mask, optional — Weighting mask.
    - returns `mean`, `p01`, `p99`, `clipLow`, `clipHigh`
- **scan**
  - `h.scan.density({ rebate, baseT }) → scanner-density — Scanner density relative to the film base: d = −log10(T / T_base), T_base = baseT when given, else the mean over the rebate box.`
    - rebate: box, px, optional — Box in source (sensor) pixels; absent means automatic.
    - baseT: vec3, fraction, [0.000001, 100], optional — Linear value of the film base (the roll's, from roll setup); wins over rebate. Absent = measure on the rebate box.
  - `h.scan.flare({ flare }) → camera-linear — Removes scanner flare: T = T′(1 + f) − f per channel, with T′ the signal relative to the open gate (after scan.flatField with an open-gate flat; ingest removeFlareValue).`
    - flare: number, percent, [0, 20], default 0 — Scanner veiling flare f, percent of the open-gate signal; [r, g, b] is per channel (ingest fitFlare / filmLayout measure it per channel).
  - `h.scan.flatField({ flat }) → camera-linear — Divides by the flat field in sensor coordinates.`
    - flat: string, optional — SHA-256 of the flat-field frame (opened like a source).
  - `h.scan.noise({ box }) → value — Measures noise σ per channel (MAD), in density.`
    - box: box, px, optional — Region; absent = whole frame.
    - returns `sigma`
  - `h.scan.rebate({ rebate }) → value — Measures the rebate (unexposed base) transmittance.`
    - rebate: box, px, optional — Box in source (sensor) pixels; absent means automatic.
    - returns `T`, `box`
- **source**
  - `h.source.info({  }) → value — Facts about the decoded source.`
    - returns `width`, `height`, `bits`, `encoding`, `sha256`
  - `h.source.xyz({ temperature_K, tint }) → scene-xyz — Photo mode: camera RGB to white-balanced scene XYZ: the camera matrix (SourceInfo.camera), then the CAT16 adaptation from the white of the temperature and tint to D65 (contract white-balance.ts sceneMatrix).`
    - temperature_K: number, K, [2000, 50000], default 6502.073737141535 — White balance: the temperature of the light the scene was lit by (Lightroom's Temperature; higher makes the picture warmer). Default: no correction (D65).
    - tint: number, [-150, 150], default 9.766663536235953 — White balance: the light's tint, green (−) to magenta (+) correction, in Lightroom's units (Adobe's: 1 = 1/3000 of a CIE 1960 uv unit across the isotemperature line).
- **view**
  - `h.view.inspect({ mode }) → display-rgb — Renders an intermediate domain for inspection (negative, dye, class views) as display RGB.`
    - mode: enum negative|density|dyes|classes|mask, default "negative" — Inspection view.

    - aim: enum grey-0.184|midgray-normalised, default "grey-0.184" — What printer lights 0 mean: the grey card prints as a neutral 0.184 reflectance (grey-0.184), or the normalised mid-grey exposure alone.

- **print**
  - `h.print.combine({ mainAmount, mainMask, terms, densities, filters, preflash }) → paper-logH — The light law of the darkroom in one node (design §22): H = T_all·(T_neg·(max(E_main − Σ E_dodge, 0) + Σ E_burn) + Σ E_flash) + Σ E_pre, with E = a·m·r·10^x per term (r = t_i / t_main in normalised mode, else 1), T_neg = 10^−Σ a·m·d, T_all = 10^Σ a·m·logH, one log at the end: x = log10 max(H, 1e-8).`
    - mainAmount: number, [0, 256], default 1 — The main exposure's amount (the receiver: the print.expose of the entry main).
    - mainMask: Mask, optional — The main exposure's coverage; absent = everywhere.
    - terms: list, default [] — Light terms besides the main exposure, each a print.expose of its own seconds and pack.
    - densities: list, default [] — Density masks d_m (print.densityMask, scalar-field): every exposure through the negative is multiplied by 10^−Σ a·m·d_m; flashes and the preflash are not.
    - filters: list, default [] — Filters in the light path: H is multiplied by 10^(Σ a·m·logH) per layer (the printer lights; a colour correction in H).
    - preflash: list, default [] — Uniform pre-exposures, added after the filters (a fraction of the grey-card exposure, H = 1 at the aim).
  - `h.print.densityMask({ gamma, radius_um, polarity }) → scalar-field — The density d_m ≥ 0 of a neutral silver mask made from the negative: H_m = blur of the negative's mean transmittance 10^−PD, with PD = x_clear − x read from the receiver (the main print.expose; x_clear its clear-film exposure).`
    - gamma: number, [0, 1], default 0 — Mask gamma γ_m (0.6: large-area contrast falls to 40 %).
    - radius_um: number, um, [0, 5000], default 500 — Gaussian σ of the blur on the film (spacer and diffuser), converted with ImageInfo.umPerPx.film.
    - polarity: enum positive|same, default "positive" — positive lowers large-area contrast (d_m = γ(log10 H_m − log10 min H_m)); same raises it (d_m = γ(log10 max H_m − log10 H_m)).
  - `h.print.develop({ paper, grade }) → paper-dyes — Develops paper log exposure to paper dye amounts through the paper curves.`
    - paper: stockId, default "kodak_portra_endura" — Colour paper.
    - grade: number, [0, 5], default 2 — Contrast grade: a gamma about the aim grey, so the grey card stays (0 → 0.7, 1 → 0.82, 2 → 1 the paper as made, 3 → 1.2, 4 → 1.45, 5 → 1.8). Colour papers have no grades; this is a contrast control (darkroom medium).
- **view**
  - `h.view.inspect({ mode }) → display-rgb — Renders an intermediate domain for inspection (negative, dye, class views) as display RGB.`
    - mode: enum negative|density|dyes|classes|mask, default "negative" — Inspection view.

## Handles in print-xyz

- **mask**
  - `h.mask.constant({ value }) → mask — A uniform mask of the receiver's size: the empty mask (0) a component fold starts from, or full coverage (1).`
    - value: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0 — The coverage everywhere (0: the empty mask, where every fold starts).
  - `h.mask.ellipse({ box, angle_deg }) → mask — Mask component 'ellipse': the ellipse inscribed in the box.`
    - box: box, px, default {"x":0,"y":0,"w":16,"h":16} — Bounding box in document px (before rotation).
    - angle_deg: number, deg, [-90, 90], default 0 — Rotation about the box centre.
  - `h.mask.linear({ from, to }) → mask — Mask component 'linear': 1 at `from`, 0 at `to`, linear between, constant beyond (a graduated burn).`
    - from: point, px, default {"x":0,"y":0} — Where the mask is 1 (document px).
    - to: point, px, default {"x":0,"y":100} — Where the mask is 0 (document px).
  - `h.mask.luminance({ above, below, softness }) → mask — Mask component 'luminance': how far the receiver's luminance (the mean of its channels, normalised to its domain range) lies inside [above, below].`
    - above: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0 — Select values above this (normalised to the domain range). 0 means no lower bound (values below the domain range stay selected).
    - below: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 1 — Select values below this. 1 means no upper bound.
    - softness: number, fraction, [0, 0.5], default 0.05 — Transition width.
  - `h.mask.paint({ strokes }) → mask — Mask component 'paint': brush strokes rasterised with soft round dabs.`
    - strokes: list, default [] — Brush strokes in order (in a document: a Coll of strokes).
  - `h.mask.radial({ box, angle_deg, feather }) → mask — Mask component 'radial': an ellipse with its own soft edge (Lightroom's radial gradient), pointwise: no blur, unlike the mask's feather.`
    - box: box, px, default {"x":0,"y":0,"w":16,"h":16} — Bounding box of the outer ellipse in document px (before rotation).
    - angle_deg: number, deg, [-90, 90], default 0 — Rotation about the box centre.
    - feather: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0.5 — Soft edge as a fraction of the radius: 1 inside the ellipse scaled by 1 − feather, 0 from the outer ellipse on, a smoothstep between.
- **measure**
  - `h.measure.densitometer({ at, aperture_px, response }) → value — Reads densities at a point, like a hand densitometer.`
    - at: point, px, default {"x":0,"y":0} — Centre in source px.
    - aperture_px: number, px, [1, 200], default 9 — Aperture diameter.
    - response: enum status-a|status-m|visual, optional — Densitometric response; absent = chosen by domain.
    - returns `D`, `visual`
  - `h.measure.histogram({ channel, bins }) → value — Histogram over the domain range.`
    - channel: enum r|g|b|L, default "L" — Channel (L = mean of channels).
    - bins: number, [8, 1024], default 64 — Number of bins.
    - returns `edges`, `counts`
  - `h.measure.patches({ box, cols, rows }) → value — Mean value per grid cell (test strips, ring-arounds, charts).`
    - box: box, px, optional — Region; absent = whole image.
    - cols: number, [1, 24], default 1 — Columns.
    - rows: number, [1, 24], default 1 — Rows.
    - returns `cells`
  - `h.measure.stats({ box, mask }) → value — Exact statistics over a region.`
    - box: box, px, optional — Region in source px; absent = whole image.
    - mask: Mask, optional — Weighting mask.
    - returns `mean`, `p01`, `p99`, `clipLow`, `clipHigh`
- **output**
  - `h.output.display({ space, rendering, knee }) → display-rgb — Turns the print's XYZ into encoded RGB in an output space.`
    - space: enum srgb|display-p3|rec2020|adobe-rgb|prophoto, default "srgb" — Output colour space (the display space for viewing; export uses Document.output.export.space).
    - rendering: enum print-as-seen|scan-of-print, default "scan-of-print" — Paper white at its own level (as seen) or at display white (scan).
    - knee: enum oklch|cam16-ucs|tanh-shoulder|clip, default "oklch" — Gamut compression; always the last colour step. 'oklch': OkLCh chroma knee (spektrafilm's parameters; called 'cam16-ucs' before contract 0.2); 'cam16-ucs': the same in CAM16-UCS (L_A 64, Y_b 20, average surround, D = 1; contract 0.3, CHB-011); 'tanh-shoulder': Chromogen's per-channel shoulder (kept for comparison; it cannot keep paper white at display white); 'clip': per channel.
- **view**
  - `h.view.adapt({ to }) → print-xyz — Chromatic adaptation of the print XYZ to the output white.`
    - to: enum D50|D65, default "D65" — White to adapt to (Document.output.white).
  - `h.view.flare({ flare }) → print-xyz — Adds viewing flare.`
    - flare: number, percent, [0, 10], default 0.48 — Viewing flare, percent of the paper white (0.48 % is the textbook value, §2.7).
  - `h.view.inspect({ mode }) → display-rgb — Renders an intermediate domain for inspection (negative, dye, class views) as display RGB.`
    - mode: enum negative|density|dyes|classes|mask, default "negative" — Inspection view.

## Handles in mask

- **mask**
  - `h.mask.combine({ other, mode, amount }) → mask — The one mask algebra (design §25): v ← v + amount·(op(v, c) − v), op add = max, subtract = v·(1 − c), intersect = v·c.`
    - other: Mask — The component (or mask) folded in.
    - mode: enum add|subtract|intersect — add: max(v, c); subtract: v·(1 − c); intersect: v·c (product forms: feathered edges meet smoothly, design D4).
    - amount: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 1 — How much the component acts: v ← v + amount·(op(v, other) − v).
  - `h.mask.constant({ value }) → mask — A uniform mask of the receiver's size: the empty mask (0) a component fold starts from, or full coverage (1).`
    - value: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0 — The coverage everywhere (0: the empty mask, where every fold starts).
  - `h.mask.ellipse({ box, angle_deg }) → mask — Mask component 'ellipse': the ellipse inscribed in the box.`
    - box: box, px, default {"x":0,"y":0,"w":16,"h":16} — Bounding box in document px (before rotation).
    - angle_deg: number, deg, [-90, 90], default 0 — Rotation about the box centre.
  - `h.mask.feather({ radius_px }) → mask — Feathers (blurs) a mask.`
    - radius_px: number, px, [0, 100000], default 10 — Feather radius in document px: a Gaussian of σ = radius/2 (the 10–90 % edge is 1.28 × radius wide). The compiler converts the mask's feather_mm on the print with the print's pitch.
  - `h.mask.invert({  }) → mask — Inverse (1 − m), an involution.`
  - `h.mask.linear({ from, to }) → mask — Mask component 'linear': 1 at `from`, 0 at `to`, linear between, constant beyond (a graduated burn).`
    - from: point, px, default {"x":0,"y":0} — Where the mask is 1 (document px).
    - to: point, px, default {"x":0,"y":100} — Where the mask is 0 (document px).
  - `h.mask.luminance({ above, below, softness }) → mask — Mask component 'luminance': how far the receiver's luminance (the mean of its channels, normalised to its domain range) lies inside [above, below].`
    - above: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0 — Select values above this (normalised to the domain range). 0 means no lower bound (values below the domain range stay selected).
    - below: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 1 — Select values below this. 1 means no upper bound.
    - softness: number, fraction, [0, 0.5], default 0.05 — Transition width.
  - `h.mask.paint({ strokes }) → mask — Mask component 'paint': brush strokes rasterised with soft round dabs.`
    - strokes: list, default [] — Brush strokes in order (in a document: a Coll of strokes).
  - `h.mask.radial({ box, angle_deg, feather }) → mask — Mask component 'radial': an ellipse with its own soft edge (Lightroom's radial gradient), pointwise: no blur, unlike the mask's feather.`
    - box: box, px, default {"x":0,"y":0,"w":16,"h":16} — Bounding box of the outer ellipse in document px (before rotation).
    - angle_deg: number, deg, [-90, 90], default 0 — Rotation about the box centre.
    - feather: number, fraction, [0, 1], default 0.5 — Soft edge as a fraction of the radius: 1 inside the ellipse scaled by 1 − feather, 0 from the outer ellipse on, a smoothstep between.
- **measure**
  - `h.measure.histogram({ channel, bins }) → value — Histogram over the domain range.`
    - channel: enum r|g|b|L, default "L" — Channel (L = mean of channels).
    - bins: number, [8, 1024], default 64 — Number of bins.
    - returns `edges`, `counts`
  - `h.measure.patches({ box, cols, rows }) → value — Mean value per grid cell (test strips, ring-arounds, charts).`
    - box: box, px, optional — Region; absent = whole image.
    - cols: number, [1, 24], default 1 — Columns.
    - rows: number, [1, 24], default 1 — Rows.
    - returns `cells`
  - `h.measure.stats({ box, mask }) → value — Exact statistics over a region.`
    - box: box, px, optional — Region in source px; absent = whole image.
    - mask: Mask, optional — Weighting mask.
    - returns `mean`, `p01`, `p99`, `clipLow`, `clipHigh`
- **output**
  - `h.output.frame({ orientation, angle_deg, crop }) → same — Crop, straighten and orientation (Document.geometry), applied last, resampling once (DR-3: all coordinates are document pixels).`
    - orientation: enum none|cw90|rot180|ccw90|flipH|flipV|transpose|transverse, default "none" — Orientation applied for display.
    - angle_deg: number, deg, [-45, 45], default 0 — Straighten: the crop content is rotated about the crop centre, clockwise as shown (after the orientation); bilinear, empty corners are 0.
    - crop: box, px, optional — Crop in document pixels of the un-oriented frame; absent = full frame. The output has the box size, oriented.
- **view**
  - `h.view.inspect({ mode }) → display-rgb — Renders an intermediate domain for inspection (negative, dye, class views) as display RGB.`
    - mode: enum negative|density|dyes|classes|mask, default "negative" — Inspection view.
